about: Witnesses for the Registry State 2 audit cluster. status: accepted = a Required test or an accepted rule states the expected outcome in the current text (V6); inferred = derived from several accepted passages, the derivation given in 'derivation'; assumption = rests on something no passage states, named in 'assumption'. Events use model/sandbox.py's vocabulary; 'expect' is checked against the model on every version, and the per-version result is in results/.

witnesses.title: An erasure that removes nothing
witnesses.source: A15 Required test 2 (V6); the historical defect (rounds 4 T12, 11 T9, 12 T7)
witnesses.observer: the owner reading the log: whether the periodic review left its trace (R0-66)
witnesses.violates_if_not: R0-66 (State 0): the erasure leaves an entry of its own naming the date

witnesses.title: Erasing before today when every entry is older
Archiving an archived project
witnesses.source: A14 Required test 2; A05 rules 1-2; A04 Required test 3
witnesses.observer: owner: the card's revision and the log

witnesses.title: A failure while storing a correction
Reading the log
witnesses.source: A14 rule 4 (Required test 4 is the agent-projection read, outside the model)

witnesses.title: A create repeated with the same request id and facts
A correction equal to the stored card
A refused confirmation, then a confirmed archive
witnesses.source: A13 rule 6, A04 rule 6 stage 1, A14 rules 2 and 5
witnesses.derivation: A refused submission is refused at stage 1 and writes no entry (A14 r2); the confirmed one changes the project and mints its id (A14 r5).

witnesses.title: The same erasure twice: no-op repeat, erasure trace and fresh numbers together
witnesses.source: the three statements of the task: a repeat writes nothing (A05 r2, A14 r3), an erasure leaves an entry (R0-66), numbers are never repeated (M09, Identity formats)
witnesses.derivation: The second erasure removes nothing, because the first erasure's entry has today's instant (A15 r4). It is not an A05 transition: A05 rule 1 is a closed list and A14 rule 3 excepts the erasure. So it writes its own entry (A15 r6) with a fresh number (A15 r5) and a fresh confirmation id (A14 r5).
witnesses.violates_if_not: R0-66 if the second leaves nothing; M09 if a number repeats

witnesses.title: Confirmation ids are never repeated
witnesses.source: Identity formats: minted per confirmation, opaque, UUID
witnesses.assumption: No passage says a confirmation id never repeats; the model mints a fresh one each time. That a random UUID is unique is a property of the format, taken here as the texts' intent.

witnesses.title: Numbering across a restore
witnesses.derivation: A restored store begins its own history from the backup's last number; within that history numbers are fresh, across histories they repeat. Earlier versions promised 'never reused' without a scope.
witnesses.actors: owner; the restore is the owner's on the host, outside Registry
witnesses.observer: owner comparing an exported log of the lost history with the new one
witnesses.violates_if_not: M09 (global reading) — resolved in R0-89 by the owner

witnesses.title: A failed change after its number was recorded
witnesses.derivation: Only meaningful where a number is recorded outside the store's transaction (V3a, V3b). From V4 the number is kept in the store, so a failed change leaves it unused and unrecorded.
witnesses.observer: owner reading the log: a gap in the numbering or not

witnesses.title: A14's equivalence after an erasure
witnesses.source: singleton topics: State 2 round 2 'Temporal scope of the audit-entry existence invariant', round 13 'Time scope of the entry-existence equivalence invariant'
witnesses.derivation: Read over the current log, the invariant says every accepted change has an entry; after an erasure an accepted change's entry is gone. Read at the change's transaction (A14 rule 1: 'in the same transaction'), it holds.
witnesses.observer: a test generated from the formal invariant (Factory), not the owner
